# Adjudication Task — Chapter 691

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃691화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|가끔 그럴 때가 있다.
  6|
  7|그날 꾸었던 꿈이 너무나도 좋아서, 그리워서 깨고 싶지 않을 때가. 일어난 후에도 한참 동안 눈을 감고 그 꿈에서 있었던 일을 곱씹을 때가.
  8|
  9|하지만 언제나 그렇듯, 세상 일은 내 바람대로 흘러가지 않는 법이다.
 10|
 11|“진태경!”
 12|
 13|- 크릉!
 14|
 15|비명 같은 외침과 함께 달려드는 두 개의 크고 작은 신형. 곧 벌어질 일을 짐작하는 건 그리 어려운 일이 아니었다.
 16|
 17|물론 그 일이 벌어지지 않게 하는 것도.
 18|
 19|탁, 풍덩!
 20|
 21|나는 신속하게 요희의 다리를 걸어 넘어트리고, 침을 질질 흘리며 다가오는 무야호의 주둥이를 밀어 냈다.
 22|
 23|그리고 한마디와 함께 다시 눈을 감았다.
 24|
 25|“삼 초. 삼 초만 건드리지 말아 봐.”
 26|
 27|속으로 셋을 셌다. 아주 느리게, 꿈속에서 봤던 모든 것을 떠올리고 머릿속에 담고 다시 눈을 떴다.
 28|
 29|동시에 밤인지, 낯인지조차 구분되지 않는 낯선 하늘이 시야에 들어온다.
 30|
 31|‘낯선 하늘이라.’
 32|
 33|이건 좀 신박하네.
 34|
 35|심심하면 보는 하늘이 낯설 수 있나 싶지만, 두 눈으로 똑똑히 보고 있는 이상 틀림없는 사실이다.
 36|
 37|나는 욱신거리는 몸을 일으키며 입을 열었다.
 38|
 39|“우선 물어볼게. 혹시 기절한 사이에 암천이 남만을 접수했다, 뭐 그런 말을 하려는 건 아니지?”
 40|
 41|연못에 넘어져 흠뻑 젖은 요희가 황당하다는 표정으로 되물었다.
 42|
 43|“눈 뜨자마자 사람 발 걸어 놓고 하는 소리가 그거니?”
 44|
 45|“눈 뜨자마자 달려드니까 발을 걸지. 그리고 하늘 봐라. 지옥이라고 해도 믿겠다.”
 46|
 47|“지옥이면 어쩌려고?”
 48|
 49|“글쎄.”
 50|
 51|나는 주위를 둘러봤다.
 52|
 53|맑은 물로 가득한 연못과 푸르른 초목(草木). 사방을 둘러싼 수풀 사이에서는 산새들의 지저귐과 짐승들의 호기심 어린 눈동자가 숨어 있다.
 54|
 55|‘지옥치고는 경치가 너무 좋은데.’
 56|
 57|내심 중얼거린 나는 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다.
 58|
 59|“이미 뒈졌는데 뭘 어떡해. 잠이나 마저 자야지.”
 60|
 61|“……잠을 자? 제정신이야?”
 62|
 63|“아니. 사실 아직도 눈앞이 어질어질해.”
 64|
 65|사실이다. 상반신을 일으킨 것만으로도 전신이 욱신거리고 현기증이 도니까.
 66|
 67|뭐 그래도…….
 68|
 69|“아직 살아 있는 것 같긴 하네. 확실하게.”
 70|
 71|그래, 나는 또 다시 살아남았다.
 72|
 73|지금 이 순간에도 엄습해 오는 고통과, 귓가에 울려 퍼지는 시스템 알림이 바로 그 증거다.
 74|
 75|띠링.
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|확인하지 못한 알림 목록이 있습니다.
 80|
 81|새로운 알림을 확인하시겠습니까?
 82|
 83|Y / N
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|곧장 시스템 창을 확인하려던 나는, 문득 잊고 있던 사실을 떠올리고 고개를 돌렸다.
 88|
 89|눈치를 보면서도 초롱초롱하게 빛나는 청백색 눈동자. 그리고 프로펠러처럼 돌아가는 꼬리를 보자 피식 웃음이 나온다.
 90|
 91|“그래, 네 덕분에 살았다.”
 92|
 93|- 크앙!
 94|
 95|와락!
 96|
 97|마치 그 말을 기다린 것처럼 무야호의 거대한 동체가 내게 달려들었다.
 98|
 99|아직 완전히 회복되지 않은 몸뚱어리가 무게에 짓눌려 비명을 질러 댔지만 괜찮다. 이건 살아 있다는 걸 알려 주는 기분 좋은 통증이니까.
100|
101|우두둑.
102|
103|“……아.”
104|
105|기분이 좀 안 좋아지려고 하네.
106|
107|
108|
109|* * *
110|
111|
112|
113|사실 암천이 아닌가 의심되는 무야호의 암살 시도는 다행히 미수에 그쳤고, 갈비뼈가 제자리에 있다는 걸 확인한 나는 가장 궁금한 점을 물었다.
114|
115|“그런데 흑웅은? 왜 안 보여?”
116|
117|동시에 볼 수 있었다. 흑웅이라는 두 글자가 나오기 무섭게 굳어 버린 요희의 얼굴을.
118|
119|“그놈 얘기는 꺼내지도 마.”
120|
121|“잠깐, 설마?”
122|
123|“그래. 네가 생각하는 그게 맞아.”
124|
125|“흑웅이 청혼했냐?”
126|
127|“……!”
128|
129|“미친놈일세. 아무리 좋아도 그렇지. 어떻게 그 상황에서 청혼을 하냐.”
130|
131|나를 미친놈 보듯 응시하던 요희가 입술을 뗐다.
132|
133|“우리가 알던 흑웅이 아니었어. 모두 속았던 거야.”
134|
135|“그렇긴 하더라. 축골공 쓰니까 나름 훈훈하던데.”
136|
137|“……축골공? 넌 알고 있었어?”
138|
139|“알고 있었지. 나한테 밀서까지 보내서 만났었는데.”
140|
141|“그럼 놈이 암천이 심어 놓은 세작(細作)이었다는 것도?”
142|
143|“당연히 그것도 알고 있, 뭐?”
144|
145|내가 지금 뭘 들은 거지.
146|
147|잠시 고민하던 나는 무겁게 입을 열었다.
148|
149|“사실이야?”
150|
151|“거짓말하는 것처럼 보여?”
152|
153|시벌, 사실인 모양이다.
154|
155|동시에 이제야 문득 추종향 추적 퀘스트가 떠올랐다.
156|
157|왜 시스템이 요희만 콕 집어 명시했었는지, 이제야 알 것 같은 기분이다.
158|
159|“좋아. 흑웅 보고 훈훈하게 생겼다고 한 건 취소. 정중한 사과도 곁들여서.”
160|
161|그 말은 하지 말걸.
162|
163|훈훈이고 나발이고, 분위기는 싸늘하게 식은 지 오래. 요희가 한숨처럼 대답했다.
164|
165|“상관없어. 덕분에 살았으니까.”
166|
167|“아, 청혼 운운한 것도 추가로 사과할게.”
168|
169|“괜찮아. 청혼한 건 사실이니까.”
170|
171|“뭐?”
172|
173|“사실이라고. 정확히는 청혼보다 명줄을 손아귀에 쥐고 흔드는 위협에 가까웠지만.”
174|
175|“그, 혹시 승낙했어?”
176|
177|“아까부터 묻고 싶었는데, 너 진짜 미친 새끼니?”
178|
179|“어, 미안. 머릿속이 복잡해서 자꾸 말이 헛나오네.”
180|
181|아직도 뒤통수가 얼얼하다.
182|
183|한때는 흑웅을 의심했던 것도 사실이지만, 독혈지에서 두 노괴(老怪)와 맞닥트린 이후에는 그 약간의 의심마저 지워 버렸었으니까.
184|
185|‘그런데 흑웅, 그 새끼가 암천의 끄나풀이었다니.’
186|
187|결국 흑웅의 역할은 소매 속의 칼이었던 셈이다. 마지막의 마지막까지 염두에 둔 남천마후의 한 수.
188|
189|그리고 이쯤에서 재차 드는 의문은, 도대체 어떻게 요희와 무야호가 그 한 수를 피했냐는 거였다.
190|
191|앞서 요희가 한 말을 들어 보면 상당히 심각한 상황에 처했던 것 같은데.
192|
193|“흑웅은 어떻게 됐지?”
194|
195|“죽었어.”
196|
197|잠시 생각하던 요희가 덧붙였다.
198|
199|“아마도.”
200|
201|“아마도?”
202|
203|“우리도 자세한 사정은 몰라. 저 백호는 목숨이 경각에 달해 있었고, 나는 놈이 준 단환에 정신을 잃었으니까. 정신을 차려 보니 이곳이었어.”
204|
205|이어지는 요희의 이야기는 짧았다. 이곳이 어디인지도, 바깥의 시간이 얼마나 흘렀는지도 모른다는 것.
206|
207|그리고 분명 숨이 끊기기 직전이었던 무야호와 중상을 입은 나는 이 신비한 연못 덕분에 살아남았다는 것.
208|
209|“이해해. 믿을 수 없는 헛소리 같겠지. 하지만 정말…….”
210|
211|“이해했어.”
212|
213|“뭐?”
214|
215|“이해했다고. 전부 다.”
216|
217|상처를 치유해 주는 연못이 뭐 그리 대수겠나.
218|
219|이런 현상을 이해할 수 없는 건 이 세상 사람들에 한해서다.
220|
221|나는 포션과 마법, 그리고 몬스터와 게이트가 존재하는 현대에서 왔고 지금 당장 저 풀숲 사이에서 오크 몇 마리가 기어 나와도 눈썹 하나 까딱하지 않을 자신이 있었다.
222|
223|“…….”
224|
225|다시 생각해 보니까 눈썹 정도는 까딱할 것 같다. 아무리 그래도 무림에서 오크가 나오는 게 정상은 아니니까.
226|
227|‘현대에서처럼 진짜 게이트가 열린다면 모를까.’
228|
229|스륵.
230|
231|내심 중얼거린 나는 손을 뻗어 잔잔한 수면 위를 훑었다.
232|
233|흡사 포션과도 같은 효력을 지닌 신비한 연못.
234|
235|아마도 내가 정신과 육체에 쌓인 피로를 금방 털어낼 수 있었던 것은, 김좌진 장군마냥 등장한 아버지 덕분만은 아니었을 것이다.
236|
237|‘아이템 감정.’
238|
239|삐빅.
240|
241|
242|
243|- 신비한 힘이 시스템을 거부합니다!
244|
245|- 해당 목표를 파악할 수 없습니다!
246|
247|
248|
249|이것 봐라.
250|
251|어느 정도는 예상했지만, 역시 알 수 없는 것들 투성이다. 하나부터 아홉까지.
252|
253|그리고 지금 막 요희의 입술 사이로 흘러나오는 열 번째 사실까지.
254|
255|“흑호(黑虎)를 봤어. 지금껏 마주한 어떤 맹수보다 강하고, 특별하게 느껴지는 검은 호랑이를.”
256|
257|“……!”
258|
259|촤륵.
260|
261|나도 모르게 흔들린 손끝이 서서히 가라앉던 수면을 뒤흔든다. 멀리 퍼져 나가는 파동을 바라보던 나는 신음을 삼켰다.
262|
263|‘애뇌산의…… 망령(亡靈).’
264|
265|단 한 번 봤지만 잊을 수 없었던 거대한 흑호가 뇌리를 스쳐 지나간다.
266|
267|망령이라는 이름답게 유령과도 같이 나타나, 유령처럼 사라지던 놈의 모습이 아직도 생생하다.
268|
269|‘그리고 그게 처음이자 마지막이었고.’
270|
271|그날 밤, 나와 야수묘왕은 망령을 쫓던 과정에서 독혈지를 발견했지만 정작 놈의 모습은 그 어디에도 발견하지 못했다.
272|
273|이는 천년지주와의 싸움이 끝난 직후 파견된 남만야수궁의 조사단도 마찬가지였고, 잇따라 벌어진 여러 굵직한 사건들로 인해 망령의 존재는 잠시 내 기억 저편에 머물러 있었다.
274|
275|그런데 놈이 지금, 여기에서 등장할 줄이야.
276|
277|‘심지어 정황을 보면 우리를 구해 준 게 틀림없는데.’
278|
279|그 의도도, 정체도 모르겠다.
280|
281|미간을 찌푸린 나는 마음속으로 중얼거렸다.
282|
283|‘알림 확인.’
284|
285|띠링.
286|
287|오직 나만이 들을 수 있는 맑은 종소리와 함께, 꾹꾹 눌러 담아져 있던 홀로그램 창들이 허공으로 뛰쳐나왔다.
288|
289|
290|
291|- 레벨 업!
292|
293|- 레벨 업의 효과로 일부 부상이 회복됩니다!
294|
295|- 레벨 업의 효과로 일부 상태 이상이 해제되었습니다!
296|
297|- 매우 뛰어난 업적, [일 대 이의 전설]을 달성하셨습니다!
298|
299|- 업적 달성 보상이 주어집니다!
300|
301|- 보너스 포인트를 획득했습니다!
302|
303|- 대량의 경험치와 명성치를 획득했습니다!
304|
305|- 돌발 퀘스트, [소매 안의 칼]이 생성되었습니다!
306|
307|- 돌발 퀘스트가 강제 취소되었습니다!
308|
309|- [???]를 발견했습니다!
310|
311|- 돌발 퀘스트, [???]가 대기 중입니다. 퀘스트 발동 조건을 모두 충족시켰을 시 진행됩니다.
312|
313|
314|
315|이제야 확인했을 뿐. 내가 정신을 잃은 사이에도 시스템은 제 역할을 톡톡히 해냈다.
316|
317|문제는 신처럼 전지전능한 시스템조차도, 내게 확실한 정보를 알려 주지 못했다는 점이다.
318|
319|‘저 물음표가 더럽게 신경 쓰이는 건 정상이겠지.’
320|
321|그리고 가장 신경 쓰이는 마지막 두 개의 알림을 뚫어져라 바라보고 있던 그때, 아까부터 자꾸 주위를 맴돌던 무야호가 내게 커다란 머리를 들이밀었다.
322|
323|- 끄으응. 끙.
324|
325|“똥 마렵니? 저기 가서 싸. 형 바쁘다.”
326|
327|- 끼이이잉.
328|
329|“바쁘다고 했…….”
330|
331|문득 말을 멈춘 나는 불현듯 고개를 들었다. 동시에 똑똑히 볼 수 있었다.
332|
333|연못을 둥그렇게 감싼 절벽 위, 아무런 기척도 없이 이곳을 내려다보는 어떤 존재를.
334|

And Yohi was about to give me one more.

[P104]
“I saw a Black Tiger. A black tiger that felt stronger and more extraordinary than any beast I’ve ever encountered.”

[P105]
“…!”

[P106]
Splash.

[P107]
My hand trembled, stirring the water as it began to settle. I watched the ripples spread and swallowed a groan.

[P108]
*The apparition of Ailao Mountain…*

[P109]
The enormous Black Tiger flashed through my mind. I’d seen it only once, but I could never forget it.

[P110]
It had appeared like a ghost, true to its name, then vanished the same way. I could still see it clearly.

[P111]
*And that was the first and last time.*

[P112]
That night, the Beast Miao King and I had discovered the Poisonblood Grounds while pursuing it, but the tiger itself had been nowhere to be found. The Nanman Beast Palace investigators sent out after the fight with the Thousand-Year Spider had found no trace of it either. Then one crisis after another had pushed it to the back of my mind.

[P113]
Now it had appeared here.

[P114]
*And from the looks of it, it saved us.*

[P115]
I didn’t know what it was or why it had done that. Frowning, I gave the System a command in my head.

[P116]
*Check notifications.*

[P117]
Ding.

[P118]
A clear bell sounded, audible only to me, and the holographic windows I’d put off checking sprang into the air.

[P119]
> **System**
>
> —Level Up!
>
> —Some injuries have healed due to the effects of Level Up!
>
> —Some Status effects have been removed due to the effects of Level Up!
>
> —You have achieved the exceptional achievement **The Legend of One Against Two**!
>
> —The achievement Reward has been granted!
>
> —You acquired bonus points!
>
> —You acquired a large amount of EXP and Fame!
>
> —A sudden Quest, **The Knife in the Sleeve**, has been created!
>
> —The sudden Quest has been forcibly canceled!
>
> —You discovered **???**!
>
> —A sudden Quest, **???**, is pending. It will begin once all activation conditions have been met!

[P120]
I was only seeing them now. The System had kept doing its job while I was unconscious.

[P121]
The problem was that even a System as all-knowing as a god couldn’t give me a straight answer.

[P122]
*Those question marks are supposed to bother the hell out of me, right?*

[P123]
I was staring at the last two notifications when Muyaho, who’d been circling me for a while, nudged me with his enormous head.

[P124]
—Nnngh. Ngh.

[P125]
“Need to poop? Go over there. Hyung’s busy.”

[P126]
—Whiiine.

[P127]
“I said I’m bu—”

[P128]
I stopped and looked up.

[P129]
Something stood atop the cliffs encircling the pond, watching us without giving off the slightest sign of its presence.

[P130]
*That’s…*

[P131]
Before I could finish the thought, a voice sounded in my head.

[P132]
—You’re awake, human.

[P133]
“…!”

[P134]
—Come up. We need to talk.

[P135]
At once, I remembered what had happened a few months ago in a broad, deep river, when an imugi that had failed to become a dragon sent its thoughts into my mind.

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
I climbed the cliff alone, leaving Yohi and Muyaho behind.

[P138]
My body was still in poor shape, but I made it to the moss-covered top. There, at last, I faced a massive Black Tiger dark as the shadows.

[P139]
The apparition of Ailao Mountain. It was the same one.

[P140]
“What… are you?”

[P141]
The Black Tiger held my gaze with eyes whose depths I couldn’t fathom.

[P142]
—I don’t know.

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
—Even I don’t know what I am. Too many years have passed for me to remember everything, and I’ve been called by many names.

[P145]
“…The apparition of Ailao Mountain.”

[P146]
—I haven’t heard that one in a long time. Has it been two hundred years?

[P147]
It sent the thought calmly and took a step. It clearly had a physical body, yet it moved like a ghost. I heard nothing and sensed no movement at all.

[P148]
Every hair on my body seemed to stand on end. Then another thought reached me.

[P149]
—But you know what kind of being I am, human.

[P150]
“…”

[P151]
—There’s no use denying it. I’ve already confirmed his existence through you.

[P152]
The Black Tiger slowly turned and opened its mouth. Between its jaws lay something brilliantly blue and clear.

[P153]
The Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence.

[P154]
“When the hell did you steal that, you bastard?”

[P155]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“What a lunatic. No matter how much he likes you, how could he propose *then*?”

[P55]
Yohi stared at me as though I were the lunatic.

[P56]
“He wasn’t the Heugung we knew. He fooled all of us.”

[P57]
“I’ll say. Once he used the Bone-Shrinking Technique, he turned out to be a pretty good-looking guy.”

[P58]
“…The Bone-Shrinking Technique? You knew?”

[P59]
“Of course. He sent me a secret letter, and we met.”

[P60]
“Then you knew Dark Heaven had planted him as a spy?”

[P61]
“Of course I knew th—what?”

[P62]
What had I just heard?

[P63]
I thought for a moment before asking, “Is that true?”

[P64]
“Do I look like I’m lying?”

[P65]
*Fuck. It’s true.*

[P66]
Only then did I remember the Quest to follow the tracking scent. Now I understood why the System had singled out Yohi by name.

[P67]
“Okay. I take back what I said about Heugung being good-looking. My apologies.”

[P68]
I shouldn’t have said it at all. To hell with his looks—the mood had gone cold long ago. Yohi answered with a sigh.

[P69]
“It doesn’t matter. I’m alive thanks to you.”

[P70]
“Oh, and I’m sorry about the proposal thing.”

[P71]
“That’s fine. He did propose.”

[P72]
“What?”

[P73]
“He did. Though it was less a proposal than a threat from someone who had my life in his hands.”

[P74]
“Did you… accept?”

[P75]
“I’ve been meaning to ask. Are you actually fucking insane?”

[P76]
“Uh, sorry. My head’s a mess. I keep saying stupid things.”

[P77]
I still felt blindsided. I’d suspected Heugung once, but after we ran into those two old monsters in the Poisonblood Grounds, I’d let even that small suspicion go.

[P78]
*And Heugung, that bastard, was working for Dark Heaven.*

[P79]
He’d been the knife in the sleeve. One last move the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had kept in reserve.

[P80]
Which raised another question: how had Yohi and Muyaho escaped him? From what Yohi had said, things had been bad.

[P81]
“What happened to Heugung?”

[P82]
“He’s dead.”

[P83]
After a moment, she added, “Probably.”

[P84]
“Probably?”

[P85]
“We don’t know exactly what happened. That White Tiger was at death’s door, and I passed out because of the pill he gave me. When I woke up, I was here.”

[P86]
The rest of her account was brief. They didn’t know where they were or how much time had passed outside. Muyaho had been moments from death, and I’d been severely injured. Both of us had survived thanks to this mysterious pond.

[P87]
“I know. It must sound impossible. But really…”

[P88]
“I get it.”

[P89]
“What?”

[P90]
“I get it. All of it.”

[P91]
What was so hard to believe about a pond that healed wounds?

[P92]
Maybe someone from this world would struggle to make sense of it. I came from a modern world with potions, Magic, monsters, and Gates. If a few Orcs crawled out of those bushes right now, I wouldn’t bat an eye.

[P93]
“…”

[P94]
On second thought, I might raise an eyebrow. Orcs appearing in Murim wouldn’t exactly be normal.

[P95]
*Unless an actual Gate opened here, like back home.*

[P96]
I reached out and skimmed the still surface of the pond.

[P97]
Its effects were much like a potion’s. My father making an entrance like General Kim Jwa-jin couldn’t have been the only reason I’d shaken off the exhaustion in my mind and body so quickly.[^1]

[P98]
*Item Appraisal.*

[P99]
Beep.

[P100]
> **System**
>
> —A mysterious power rejects the System!
>
> —The target cannot be identified!

[P101]
There it was.

[P102]
I’d expected as much. Everything about this place was a mystery, from one thing to the next.

[P103]
And Yohi was about to give me one more.

[P104]
“I saw a Black Tiger. A black tiger that felt stronger and more extraordinary than any beast I’ve ever encountered.”

[P105]
“…!”

[P106]
Splash.

[P107]
My hand trembled, stirring the water as it began to settle. I watched the ripples spread and swallowed a groan.

[P108]
*The apparition of Ailao Mountain…*

[P109]
The enormous Black Tiger flashed through my mind. I’d seen it only once, but I could never forget it.

[P110]
It had appeared like a ghost, true to its name, then vanished the same way. I could still see it clearly.

[P111]
*And that was the first and last time.*

[P112]
That night, the Beast Miao King and I had discovered the Poisonblood Grounds while pursuing it, but the tiger itself had been nowhere to be found. The Nanman Beast Palace investigators sent out after the fight with the Thousand-Year Spider had found no trace of it either. Then one crisis after another had pushed it to the back of my mind.

[P113]
Now it had appeared here.

[P114]
*And from the looks of it, it saved us.*

[P115]
I didn’t know what it was or why it had done that. Frowning, I gave the System a command in my head.

[P116]
*Check notifications.*

[P117]
Ding.

[P118]
A clear bell sounded, audible only to me, and the holographic windows I’d put off checking sprang into the air.

[P119]
> **System**
>
> —Level Up!
>
> —Some injuries have healed due to the effects of Level Up!
>
> —Some Status effects have been removed due to the effects of Level Up!
>
> —You have achieved the exceptional achievement **The Legend of One Against Two**!
>
> —The achievement Reward has been granted!
>
> —You acquired bonus points!
>
> —You acquired a large amount of EXP and Fame!
>
> —A sudden Quest, **The Knife in the Sleeve**, has been created!
>
> —The sudden Quest has been forcibly canceled!
>
> —You discovered **???**!
>
> —A sudden Quest, **???**, is pending. It will begin once all activation conditions have been met!

[P120]
I was only seeing them now. The System had kept doing its job while I was unconscious.

[P121]
The problem was that even a System as all-knowing as a god couldn’t give me a straight answer.

[P122]
*Those question marks are supposed to bother the hell out of me, right?*

[P123]
I was staring at the last two notifications when Muyaho, who’d been circling me for a while, nudged me with his enormous head.

[P124]
—Nnngh. Ngh.

[P125]
“Need to poop? Go over there. Hyung’s busy.”

[P126]
—Whiiine.

[P127]
“I said I’m bu—”

[P128]
I stopped and looked up.

[P129]
Something stood atop the cliffs encircling the pond, watching us without giving off the slightest sign of its presence.

[P130]
*That’s…*

[P131]
Before I could finish the thought, a voice sounded in my head.

[P132]
—You’re awake, human.

[P133]
“…!”

[P134]
—Come up. We need to talk.

[P135]
At once, I remembered what had happened a few months ago in a broad, deep river, when an imugi that had failed to become a dragon sent its thoughts into my mind.

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
I climbed the cliff alone, leaving Yohi and Muyaho behind.

[P138]
My body was still in poor shape, but I made it to the moss-covered top. There, at last, I faced a massive Black Tiger dark as the shadows.

[P139]
The apparition of Ailao Mountain. It was the same one.

[P140]
“What… are you?”

[P141]
The Black Tiger held my gaze with eyes whose depths I couldn’t fathom.

[P142]
—I don’t know.

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
—Even I don’t know what I am. Too many years have passed for me to remember everything, and I’ve been called by many names.

[P145]
“…The apparition of Ailao Mountain.”

[P146]
—I haven’t heard that one in a long time. Has it been two hundred years?

[P147]
It sent the thought calmly and took a step. It clearly had a physical body, yet it moved like a ghost. I heard nothing and sensed no movement at all.

[P148]
Every hair on my body seemed to stand on end. Then another thought reached me.

[P149]
—But you know what kind of being I am, human.

[P150]
“…”

[P151]
—There’s no use denying it. I’ve already confirmed his existence through you.

[P152]
The Black Tiger slowly turned and opened its mouth. Between its jaws lay something brilliantly blue and clear.

[P153]
The Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence.

[P154]
“When the hell did you steal that, you bastard?”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

He’d been the knife in the sleeve. One last move the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had kept in reserve.

[P80]
Which raised another question: how had Yohi and Muyaho escaped him? From what Yohi had said, things had been bad.

[P81]
“What happened to Heugung?”

[P82]
“He’s dead.”

[P83]
After a moment, she added, “Probably.”

[P84]
“Probably?”

[P85]
“We don’t know exactly what happened. That White Tiger was at death’s door, and I passed out because of the pill he gave me. When I woke up, I was here.”

[P86]
The rest of her account was brief. They didn’t know where they were or how much time had passed outside. Muyaho had been moments from death, and I’d been severely injured. Both of us had survived thanks to this mysterious pond.

[P87]
“I know. It must sound impossible. But really…”

[P88]
“I get it.”

[P89]
“What?”

[P90]
“I get it. All of it.”

[P91]
What was so hard to believe about a pond that healed wounds?

[P92]
Maybe someone from this world would struggle to make sense of it. I came from a modern world with potions, Magic, monsters, and Gates. If a few Orcs crawled out of those bushes right now, I wouldn’t bat an eye.

[P93]
“…”

[P94]
On second thought, I might raise an eyebrow. Orcs appearing in Murim wouldn’t exactly be normal.

[P95]
*Unless an actual Gate opened here, like back home.*

[P96]
I reached out and skimmed the still surface of the pond.

[P97]
Its effects were much like a potion’s. My father making an entrance like General Kim Jwa-jin couldn’t have been the only reason I’d shaken off the exhaustion in my mind and body so quickly.[^1]

[P98]
*Item Appraisal.*

[P99]
Beep.

[P100]
> **System**
>
> —A mysterious power rejects the System!
>
> —The target cannot be identified!

[P101]
There it was.

[P102]
I’d expected as much. Everything about this place was a mystery, from one thing to the next.

[P103]
And Yohi was about to give me one more.

[P104]
“I saw a Black Tiger. A black tiger that felt stronger and more extraordinary than any beast I’ve ever encountered.”

[P105]
“…!”

[P106]
Splash.

[P107]
My hand trembled, stirring the water as it began to settle. I watched the ripples spread and swallowed a groan.

[P108]
*The apparition of Ailao Mountain…*

[P109]
The enormous Black Tiger flashed through my mind. I’d seen it only once, but I could never forget it.

[P110]
It had appeared like a ghost, true to its name, then vanished the same way. I could still see it clearly.

[P111]
*And that was the first and last time.*

[P112]
That night, the Beast Miao King and I had discovered the Poisonblood Grounds while pursuing it, but the tiger itself had been nowhere to be found. The Nanman Beast Palace investigators sent out after the fight with the Thousand-Year Spider had found no trace of it either. Then one crisis after another had pushed it to the back of my mind.

[P113]
Now it had appeared here.

[P114]
*And from the looks of it, it saved us.*

[P115]
I didn’t know what it was or why it had done that. Frowning, I gave the System a command in my head.

[P116]
*Check notifications.*

[P117]
Ding.

[P118]
A clear bell sounded, audible only to me, and the holographic windows I’d put off checking sprang into the air.

[P119]
> **System**
>
> —Level Up!
>
> —Some injuries have healed due to the effects of Level Up!
>
> —Some Status effects have been removed due to the effects of Level Up!
>
> —You have achieved the exceptional achievement **The Legend of One Against Two**!
>
> —The achievement Reward has been granted!
>
> —You acquired bonus points!
>
> —You acquired a large amount of EXP and Fame!
>
> —A sudden Quest, **The Knife in the Sleeve**, has been created!
>
> —The sudden Quest has been forcibly canceled!
>
> —You discovered **???**!
>
> —A sudden Quest, **???**, is pending. It will begin once all activation conditions have been met!

[P120]
I was only seeing them now. The System had kept doing its job while I was unconscious.

[P121]
The problem was that even a System as all-knowing as a god couldn’t give me a straight answer.

[P122]
*Those question marks are supposed to bother the hell out of me, right?*

[P123]
I was staring at the last two notifications when Muyaho, who’d been circling me for a while, nudged me with his enormous head.

[P124]
—Nnngh. Ngh.

[P125]
“Need to poop? Go over there. Hyung’s busy.”

[P126]
—Whiiine.

[P127]
“I said I’m bu—”

[P128]
I stopped and looked up.

[P129]
Something stood atop the cliffs encircling the pond, watching us without giving off the slightest sign of its presence.

[P130]
*That’s…*

[P131]
Before I could finish the thought, a voice sounded in my head.

[P132]
—You’re awake, human.

[P133]
“…!”

[P134]
—Come up. We need to talk.

[P135]
At once, I remembered what had happened a few months ago in a broad, deep river, when an imugi that had failed to become a dragon sent its thoughts into my mind.

[P136]
* * *

[P137]
I climbed the cliff alone, leaving Yohi and Muyaho behind.

[P138]
My body was still in poor shape, but I made it to the moss-covered top. There, at last, I faced a massive Black Tiger dark as the shadows.

[P139]
The apparition of Ailao Mountain. It was the same one.

[P140]
“What… are you?”

[P141]
The Black Tiger held my gaze with eyes whose depths I couldn’t fathom.

[P142]
—I don’t know.

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
—Even I don’t know what I am. Too many years have passed for me to remember everything, and I’ve been called by many names.

[P145]
“…The apparition of Ailao Mountain.”

[P146]
—I haven’t heard that one in a long time. Has it been two hundred years?

[P147]
It sent the thought calmly and took a step. It clearly had a physical body, yet it moved like a ghost. I heard nothing and sensed no movement at all.

[P148]
Every hair on my body seemed to stand on end. Then another thought reached me.

[P149]
—But you know what kind of being I am, human.

[P150]
“…”

[P151]
—There’s no use denying it. I’ve already confirmed his existence through you.

[P152]
The Black Tiger slowly turned and opened its mouth. Between its jaws lay something brilliantly blue and clear.

[P153]
The Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence.

[P154]
“When the hell did you steal that, you bastard?”

[P155]
[^1]: Kim Jwa-jin (1889–1930) was a Korean independence activist and military commander.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
